rows.verification_scope: Root 5.0.1 is the current release intent, superseding 5.0.0 for release-note provenance. Root metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CITATION.cff`, the release note and its overview art declare 5.0.1, and `check_release_versions.py` passes with root 5.0.1 across all 25 exemplars. Two tags are named here, and which one supersedes matters. The `v5.0.0` tag is `e932a5d2a4f5c75f354352b43e54039eac9f63cf` (annotated `9829f410cf1d4edddcefb5374363f11ef366044d`); its in-tree copy of `docs/releases/v5.0.0.md` names `c5af32a18560ca12267484b182a94b826b47cf47` as the tagged commit, which is false — that is the `#215` merge, an intermediate release-train merge 44 commits before the tag — and the tag is not moved and not re-cut. The `v5.0.1` tag is `3617740049de0f146329c5222a62b41494ca2203` (annotated `c6aae549c334b0ee55a153e5b85c27278b70dd35`), the merge of the release-train pull request that carries the corrected note and the fail-closed release-notes tag-commit check that refuses that defect; `v5.0.1` supersedes `v5.0.0` for note provenance, the root release contract passes at that revision, and the repository's required `CI Gate` is green on that exact commit. The hosted required-acceptance lane has not run at the `v5.0.1` revision and remains the open item: ordinary CI and the root contract are not that lane, so no acceptance or publication step may be treated as satisfied.

rows.subsystem: Root release boundary (`pyproject.toml`, tags, GitHub releases, `CHANGELOG.md`)
rows.verification_scope: Root 5.0.2 is the current release intent, superseding 5.0.1 for rendered-provenance and release-note provenance. Root metadata, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CITATION.cff`, the release note and its overview art declare 5.0.2, and the coordinated transaction moved all 25 exemplars' SDK requirement, `[tool.template].platform_version` binding and lock to 5.0.2 while retaining exemplar own versions; the fifteen exemplars that track a publication copy were re-rendered and re-receipted and the other ten were rebound. The post-merge rebind automation (`.github/workflows/rebind.yml`) restamps receipts as its own commit and runs both strict publication gates on the committed tree before any push; it is dispatch-only until the owner provisions a protected-branch bypass for the pushing identity. The ceremony adopts the invariant that the tag must be cut at a commit whose tree equals the verified tree, and both publication gates at the tag are the release verdict; the `v5.0.1` tag is not moved and not re-cut, and 5.0.2 supersedes it. The hosted required-acceptance lane has not run at the 5.0.2 revision and remains the open item: ordinary CI and the root contract are not that lane, so no acceptance or publication step may be treated as satisfied.
